q: Where is Paul as he writes this letter?
a: Paul is in prison as he writes this letter.

q: To whom is this letter written?
a: This letter is written to Philemon, Paul’s dear friend and fellow-worker.

q: In what kind of place is the church meeting?
a: The church is meeting in a house.

q: According to Paul, what has Philemon done for the saints?
a: Philemon has refreshed the hearts of the saints.

q: Why is Paul asking Philemon for something instead of commanding him?
a: Paul is asking Philemon because of love.

q: Where was Paul when he became Onesimus’ father?
a: Paul was in chains, in prison.

q: What has Paul done with Onesimus?
a: Paul has sent Onesimus back to Philemon.

q: Where is Paul as he writes this letter?
a: Paul is in prison as he writes this letter.

q: What would Paul like Onesimus to be able to do?
a: Paul would like Onesimus to be able to help him.

q: Why did Paul not want to act without the consent of Philemon?
a: Paul wanted Philemon’s good deed to be his own choice and not forced upon him by Paul’s action.

q: Why did Paul say Onesimus may have been separated from Philemon?
a: Paul said Onesimus may have been separated from Philemon so that Philemon could have him back forever, meaning as an eternal brother in Christ.

q: How does Paul now want Philemon to consider Onesimus?
a: Paul wants Philemon to consider Onesimus as a beloved brother.

q: What does Paul want Philemon to do about anything that Onesimus owes Philemon?
a: Paul wants Philemon to charge anything owed by Onesimus to Paul’s account.
Philemon owes Paul his very life.

q: What does Paul want Philemon to do for him?
a: Paul wants Philemon to prepare a guest room for him.

q: Why does Paul want Philemon to do this?
a: Paul hopes that God will send him back to Philemon.
